key_facts: Subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion 4 days prior to presentation
3 hours of substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Initial serum troponin I level of 6.18 ng/mL
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of chest pressure radiating to the jaw, diaphoresis, and vomiting, along with ECG findings of ST-segment elevations and PR-segment depression, and elevated inflammatory markers, are consistent with acute pericarditis. The normal coronary angiography and transthoracic echocardiogram results also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Myopericarditis
rejected.why: While myopericarditis could explain some of the symptoms, the normal echocardiogram and lack of significant left ventricular dysfunction make it less likely than acute pericarditis.

rejected.label: Acute myocarditis
rejected.why: The patient's normal cardiac examination, normal left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, and normal transthoracic echocardiogram results make acute myocarditis less likely, despite the elevated troponin level, which can also be seen in acute pericarditis.
